Name: Realistic Seasonal Shop Inventory - No More Unlimited Stock
Author: boringvlln
Description:
[right][size=1]Has it ever bothered you...
What would Jodi, or Sam, or Pam even [i]buy at the store[/i], when it's all about seeds and farming supplies?
How is it that Pierre never [i]runs out of seeds[/i] to sell?
How come Willy or Marnie never sell the [i]products they produce[/i] to you?
[/size][/right][right][size=1]Inspired by [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10826]Pierre's Roulette Shop[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/24195]No Seeds For Coin - Seed Shortage[/url]﻿, and [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10598]Shop Overhaul Compilation[/url]﻿.﻿
[/size][/right]


[center][size=3]Requires [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1915]Content Patcher[/url] [/size][/center]
This mod aims to carefully [u]expand the range[/u] of items available at stores, while also [u]liming the amount of items[/u] available.

Main rules are:

1. Vendors sell a wider range of items, sensible to their profession, and target other characters besides the player.
2. Items vary by season.
3. Items are not as predictable, many of them are available randomly.
4. The amount of items available is restricted.

Every shop has a settings that can be set to "Standard", "Hardmode", or "off".

"Hardmode" comes with lower stock amount, sometimes higher prices and lower chances of rare items. Changes to every shop can be disabled individually. Compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url].


[size=3][center][b]Saloon
[/b][/center][/size]
Gus is trying to cut costs to make ends meet, so he primarily [u]cooks from seasonal ingredients[/u] to save up.

Prepare for [color=#00ff00]Parsnip Soup[/color] in the spring, [color=#ff00ff]Pink Cake[/color] in the summer, [color=#ff7700]Pumpkin Pie[/color] in the fall, and [color=#00ffff]Trout Soup[/color] in the winter (just some examples, actual variety is bigger, [color=#ffff00]random [/color]rotation).
There are also some dishes available year round too, such as Pancakes.
Additionally, he serves alcohol, caffeinated drinks (and occasional Ginger Ale too).
He is but one man, so the amount of food he is able to cook is not limitless. He serves more food on the weekend, starting with Friday. And his stock can increase after certain events.

[center][b][size=3]Pierre's General Store
[/size][/b][/center]
Pierre aims his store to be the one-stop shop of the town (but maybe falls a little short).

He sells [color=#00ff00]seasonal [/color]seeds (expanded amount, including Strawberry Seeds starting from [b]Year 2[/b], as well as the new 1.6 added seeds).
But the seeds rotate on a [color=#ffff00]random[/color] basis and the stock is limited. Meaning you may arrive to the shop in the spring to only find 20 Parsnip Seeds, and will have to come back tomorrow to have a [i]chance [/i]to buy some Kale Seeds instead.

His stock starts as more limited, but can increase after a certain event.

Those without a green thumb come here to buy Bread, sauces, Flour, Sugar and such (also limited amount in stock), or [b]seasonal vegetables[/b] and flowers (much less of the latter).

Caroline also helps out the family business now, by offering some Tea Leaves for sale from time to time.

[b][size=3][center]Festivals[/center][/size][/b]
Items from Pierre's stands are far less predictable and rotate [color=#ffff00]randomly[/color] (except for the Stardew Fair, the one with tokens, it is left as it was).

Notable changes: instead of Strawberry Seeds Pierre now sells [u]actual[/u] Strawberry. (Seeds are sometimes available at the shop instead.)
There is also Green Tea available as a refreshment.

[size=3][b][center]Adventurer's Guild[/center][/b][/size]
Marlon has positively decided that adventurers need help taking care of themselves, so he now sells Life Elixir and Garlic Oil (limited amount per day).

He also sometimes offers a [color=#ffff00]random [/color][u]Mineral and Gem[/u] (for a completely unreasonable rip-off price, but don't tell him that). So if you are looking for a gift, or need help with the Museum's collection, he can help you out (he does [b]not [/b]sell anything impossibly rare).

Additionally, he has a bit of [u]monster loot[/u] to spare. Another notable change: a certain special weapon can no longer be obtain for money, and instead requires a rare item.

[size=3][b][center]Marnie's Ranch[/center][/b][/size]
Marnie now does not have an impossibly large amount of hay to spare. She has some, but maybe it's time for a Silo.

She offers a moderate amount of various [u]Milk, Eggs, and Cheese[/u], with occasional extras.

More complex items for sale are now more rare and on [color=#ffff00]random [/color]rotation, she is running a ranch after all. Swing by her house more often if you desire a Dog House or require a Heater, don't count on it being in stock every day.

[size=3][b][center]Blacksmith[/center][/b][/size]
Clint would rather sell you [u]Metal Bars[/u] and not ores. He is smelting them for a living after all. He has Copper, Iron, and Gold Bars in stock (a little ore on [color=#ffff00]rotation [/color]too, but he doesn't like to share).

Additionally, he now sells Lightning Rods, Batteries, Starting and Quality [u]Sprinklers[/u] (only those two levels, no higher), Iron Fences, and... [u][url=https://youtu.be/NhsK5WExrnE]Bombs[/url][/u].
Marlon still doesn't trust him to make weapons for some reason...

Some of Clint's items for sale depend on your progress in the mines, or even weather.

[size=3][b][center]Carpenter's Shop[/center][/b][/size]

Decorating the house has never been so[u] immersively inconvenient[/u]. Furniture has been divided into categories and [color=#ffff00]randomized[/color], what shall Robin have in stock tomorrow - nobody knows. The amount of items is also limited, as she can can only make so many items.
She also sells big craftables (machines).
As for the materials, Robin can not be bothered to spare the materials she needs on her craft, so she only sells a very limited amount.

Her stock varies depending on the day of the week! See spoiler, if you want to know.
[spoiler]
Every day: Wood, Stone, a random big craftable. Monday - Dividers, Logs, Bookcases. Wednesday - Beds, Tables, Fireplaces. Thursday - Stools, Benches, Dressers. Friday - Lamps, Chairs, Windows. Saturday - Paintings and Armchairs. Sunday - Workbench (a random chance), Couches, Rugs, Electronics.[/spoiler]


[size=3][b][center]Casino[/center][/b][/size]
This part of the mod is an outlier, has nothing to do with limiting the stock, and therefore is [u]disabled by default[/u].
Only adds [color=#9900ff]Treasure Chest as a reward for 500 QI coins[/color], allowing you to exhange your winnings for money (by selling said chest for 5k Gold).

It is basically an updated version of [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/11895]Treasure Chest at Casino[/url] by Schneitizel. If you want the higher difficulty of the original mod, set "Casino" to "hardmode" in config.

[size=3][b][center]Dwarf[/center][/b][/size]
No longer sells bombs, but is willing to share some juicy [u]Bug Steaks[/u] instead. Also has a little of [color=#ffff00]random[/color] small loot to share, including monster loot.
Offers either one or the other decorative item he normally has, randomly. Still offers Elixirs, but in much restricted quantity.

[size=3][b][center]Fish Shop[/center][/b][/size]
Willy sells a reasonable amount (!) of random common (!) [u]Fishes[/u] of the [color=#00ff00]season[/color]. He also sells some Algae of random variety, and a small amount of bait.
Fishing related stock is limited in number and [color=#ffff00]randomized [/color](which bobber will he have in stock - nobody knows).

[size=3][b][center]Hospital and Ice Cream Stand[/center][/b][/size]
Nothing unusual here, except for the [u]limited[/u] amount of remedies available per day.

[size=3][b][center]Ginger island Resort Bar[/center][/b][/size]
Is essentially a much smaller version of the [u]Saloon[/u] inventory. Gus still cooks [color=#00ff00]seasonal [/color]food, but he doesn't bring that much with him.
No Mango Wine, varied drinks instead.

[size=3][b][center]Sandy's Oasis[/center][/b][/size]
Sandy sells [color=#00ff00]seasonal [/color]seeds for a pretty penny (how many farmers you reckon come by the place?). That includes possible Coffee Beans, too.
For the common traveler she offers a small stock of snacks instead.
Her furniture items rotate [color=#ffff00]randomly[/color].
If you are on the lookout for a seasonal plant, she has them all (but you'll never know which one).

[size=3][b][center]Krobus and his Shadow Shop[/center][/b][/size]
More item amount limitations, some items are [color=#ffff00]randomized.[/color] Heftier price on a [i]creepy[/i] new item from 1.6.

[size=3][b][center]Joja[/center][/b][/size]
They have [u]the largest stock[/u]. The seeds available are still [color=#ffff00]randomized [/color]and [color=#00ff00]seasonal[/color].
They have vegetables, both seasonal and off-season (the latter being pricier, of course).
They have Fish (a little), Eggs (not large ones), Milk (only Cow Milk). As well as other groceries too, as usual (no Tea Leaves, however).
[color=#660000]How could you possibly resist the temptation to shop there?..
[/color]

[size=3][b][center][u]Compatibility[/u][/center][/b][/size]
Unfortunately, since this is a very manual edit, mods adding new items to shops would need to be patched to fit in ([i]unless [/i]the author/s already made their items limited in amount, which is so very fantastic and compatible by default).

For more details on the patches see their changelog. All patches can be used independently from the main RSSI file. Every patch has its own version history, which has nothing to do with the main file version.
